{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --time=01:00:00
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=18
#   --mem=8G
#   --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#   --output="laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out"

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 18 \
  --time=1h \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm --output by redirecting stdout/stderr.
exec >"laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out" 2>&1

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=8G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-node=18 cannot be expressed portably in Flux here.
# Performance implication: tasks may be mapped differently across resources (though N=1 here), which can affect
# CPU binding/locality and performance.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name="glap_bol_lin" is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module load matlab/R2022a
module load intel
export omp_num_threads=8

cd /home/lynch/boltzmann_solvers/mtmhbe_solver/performance/laporta/grid_study/nvib_sweep_data/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "laporta_bolsig_linear;exit;"
'
"
}
